title: Deep Neural Network Architectures for Financial Forecasting: A Comparative Study of DNN, LSTM, and GRU
tldr: Compares DNN, LSTM, and GRU architectures for stock price and financial index forecasting, finding that a hybrid CNN-LSTM-GRU architecture achieves 2.3% lower MAPE than the best individual model.
problem_and_motivation: Financial time-series forecasting is critical for personal investment decisions but challenging due to non-stationarity, volatility, and complex temporal dependencies. Individual neural architectures have complementary strengths but no single architecture consistently outperforms.
approach: Compared four architectures: standard DNN, LSTM, GRU, and Hybrid CNN-LSTM-GRU.
Dataset: daily closing prices for S&P 500, NASDAQ, and three individual stocks (2010-2024).
Hybrid model: CNN layers for local feature extraction → LSTM for long-term dependencies → GRU for short-term patterns.
Preprocessing: Min-Max normalization, sliding window of 60 days for sequence input.
Evaluation: RMSE, MAPE, MAE, and Directional Accuracy (DA).
Statistical significance testing using Diebold-Mariano test.
findings: num: Hybrid CNN-LSTM-GRU achieved lowest MAPE (1.87%) vs. GRU (2.41%), LSTM (2.53%), DNN (3.12%).
num: Directional accuracy of hybrid model: 68.3% vs. GRU 63.1% and LSTM 61.5%.
CNN layers effectively extract local price patterns and volatility regimes before sequence modeling.
Hybrid model shows particular improvement during high-volatility periods (35% lower error vs. individual models).
Bayesian hyperparameter optimization improved all models by 8-12% over default settings.
All models degrade in performance beyond 30-day forecast horizon; hybrid model degrades most slowly.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides clear evidence that hybrid architectures combining CNN (local features), LSTM (long-term dependencies), and GRU (short-term patterns) outperform individual models for financial time-series forecasting. The hybrid model's robustness during high-volatility periods is particularly relevant for PFMS operating in emerging markets. The Bayesian optimization methodology is transferable to PFMS model development.
directly_justifies: Hybrid CNN-LSTM-GRU outperforms individual DNN, LSTM, and GRU for financial forecasting.
CNN layers improve feature extraction from financial time-series.
Hybrid models show particular advantage during high-volatility periods.
Bayesian hyperparameter optimization improves model performance by 8-12%.
limits: Focused on stock/ index prices, not personal income/expense forecasting. [acknowledged]
No evaluation on individual-level financial data. [unacknowledged]
Computational cost of hybrid model not compared. [unacknowledged]
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domains 6.B (income/expense forecasting) and 14.A (ML approaches) were flagged as highly relevant because the paper compares neural architectures for financial time-series forecasting. Domain 6.A was flagged as medium relevance because the methodology applies to spending prediction. Domains 1-5, 7-13, 14.B were rejected as the paper focuses on financial index forecasting without personal finance user aspects or PFMS-specific modules.

limitations: No evaluation on individual-level transaction data. [unacknowledged]
